candidates.summary: Passing a []T as ...I is still accepted: the variadic-slice branch recurses into assignability, the same shape the diff removed from the pointer branch, so a callee can write a non-T value into the caller's []T
candidates.failure_scenario: type I interface{ M() int }; T{x int} and U{s string} both implement I; func f(xs ...I) { xs[0] = U{"hello"} }; ts := []T{{1}}; f(ts...); println(ts[0].x, ts[0].M()). Go rejects at compile time (cannot use ts (variable of type []T) as []I value). Gno at head compiles it and prints "hello" for the int field ts[0].x and 5 for ts[0].M(): the caller's []T now holds a U value, and a realm's typed slice can be corrupted the same way, persisted. The ADR names the pointer sibling (*int to *interface{}) as the reason for the rewrite; this member of the same class predates the diff (base type_check.go:577-578) and the sweep missed it.

candidates.summary: Runtime interface assertions now walk the whole method signature structurally for a flat gas charge, so a realm can buy ~100x more validator CPU per unit of gas than at the merge base
candidates.failure_scenario: VerifyImplementedBy runs on every x.(I), comma-ok assert, interface type-switch case and Stringer/error check while printing; it is charged OpCPUTypeAssert1/2 plus 349 per interface method. At base the per-method check compared two cached TypeID strings; at head identicalTypes(mt, im.Type) recurses through every field of every param/result type each call, since the interface's and the method's signature types are separate objects. A package declaring I with M(s struct{...nested fields...}) and T.M spelling the same literal, looping 20000 x.(I), uses the same gas (42.886M) for 0.02s with a 1-field param and 0.53s with 2000 leaf fields (36 KB source), 2.56s with 10000 (181 KB): block time per gas grows ~25-128x, against ~60x less work for the same input at base (cached TypeID compare: 2.3us vs 140us per check at 10000 fields).

candidates.summary: A := redeclaration to a type differing only in struct tags, embeddedness or variadicity is still accepted and silently changes the variable's static type; the diff moved the sibling 'Redefinition cannot change .T' check to identicalTypes but left StaticBlock.Define2 on TypeID
candidates.failure_scenario: x := struct{A int "a"}{}; y, x := 1, struct{A int "b"}{2}: Go rejects (cannot use struct{A int "b"}{…} as struct{A int "a"} value in assignment); Gno at head accepts and prints "2 1". With f := func(xs []int){}; y, f := 1, func(xs ...int){}; f([]int{7,8,9}), the redeclaration is accepted and the later call fails with "cannot use []int as int": f's static type changed from func([]int) to func(...int) mid-scope. A non-variant type (x := 1; y, x := 1, "s") is rejected by Define2, so only the identity-only differences the PR targets slip through.
